messages:
maya: quick note 10: working on UI to let customers pick SLO fallback policies from the console. prototype toggles for granularity + notify-order. put up a tiny demo.
ben: nice. are we going route-level editable or locked to tenant/global? route-level could be a lot of churn.
maya: prototype supports three levels: global (company-wide), tenant (per-org), and route (per-endpoint). default is tenant. we're debating whether to expose route-edit for large tenants.
rachel: from API POV we currently have notify_fallbacks on the SLO object. do you plan to replace it?
maya: not replace. plan: keep legacy fields but add a routing_policy object that can optionally override notify_fallbacks and attach a quota_label. reads synthesize legacy for backward compat. writes accept both shapes for grace period.
sam: preview is the bigger ask. people want to know if changing fallback order will dramatically increase pager volume. how accurate does the preview need to be?
lee: realistic enough to show relative delta and an upper bound. we should show both absolute expected notifications/day and a percent change vs baseline. add a confidence interval if possible.
ben: implementation notes: preview will sample recent SLO hit history and cross-reference subscription lists. expensive if done naively for tenants with millions of hits.
maya: implementation idea: async preview job with sampling window + reservoir sampling. cache results per-tenant+policy for 45m. UI shows cached result or "running" state. preview cost charged to tenant credits.
rachel: API sketch suggestion: POST /v1/slo/{slo_id}/routing_policy_preview with body {"routing_policy": {...}, "sample_window": "24h"}. response is job id + estimated numbers once ready.
maya: yes along those lines. quick sketch: ```json
POST /api/v1/slo/12345/routing_policy_preview
{
  "routing_policy": {
    "label": "quiet-default-v2",
    "quota_label": "q:acme:quiet",
    "notify_order": ["email","slack","pagerduty"],
    "level": "tenant"
  },
  "sample_window": "24h"
}
```
then GET /api/v1/preview_jobs/{job_id} returns status + estimates.
sam: two operational concerns: 1) telemetry spike when everyone requests preview, 2) accidental flips causing real notify changes mid-day.
lee: mitigate 1 with server-side rate limit per-tenant and per-user. mitigate 2 with an apply-confirm step and an audit prompt.
ben: audit is required. legal requested change history retention. we should record old vs new routing_policy, who applied, and feature-flag context. store in change_logs with a small schema bump (routing_policy_blob, apply_from_user).
maya: agree. also add an "apply_dry_run" endpoint that persists nothing but writes a changelog entry with dry_run=true for traceability.
rachel: backwards compatibility: GET slo should still return top-level notify_fallbacks for older clients. we'll synthesize from routing_policy when present. document this clearly.
ben: telemetry events during rollout: routing_policy_edit, preview_requested, preview_ready, routing_policy_applied, routing_policy_apply_failed. include tenant_id, editor_id, job_id, estimated_notify_delta.
sam: add SLOs on apply path: 95th pct apply latency < 2s for simple edits, but for bulk route edits we should have an async apply with progress.
lee: for large bulk operations return a job id and notify UI via websockets once complete. add a cancellation endpoint for long-running applies.
maya: gating: only org-admins can change notify order. route-level edits require an extra confirmation modal that lists affected routes and estimated pager delta.
ben: rollout plan: feature-flagged server-side, opt-in toggle in console for teams, 10% canary for 3 days with telemetry review, then ramp to 50% then 100%. SRE to run soak test on preview service.
maya: UI details: coalesce rapid edits in the client (500ms debounce) and server-side coalesce (30s) with last-write-wins. show a diff preview in the modal.
lee: preview math: return absolute estimate, relative percent, 90% CI, and an upper-bound scenario if subscription lists include on-call escalation.
sam: cost note: previews will consume compute; add a quick visible estimate of "preview cost" in credits to discourage frivolous runs.
maya: good call. add a small UX nudge explaining cached previews and TTL.
ben: final ask: add a flag so platform team can disable previews for specific tenants if performance or policy reasons.
maya: will include in RFC. I'll open RFC with API schema, DB changes, telemetry events, rollout checklist, and a short simulator doc for SRE review. tagging @rachel @ben @sam @lee.
deploy-bot: Tip: use the ff-rollout checklist at https://internal/ff-rollout and include an obs playbook. :robot_face:
san: thanks all, will read RFC and schedule a quick SRE sync.
